# SAFE Rave Coffee public-evidence extract — owned surfaces

Captured 2026-09-06 for internal strategic research only. Rave Coffee did not supply or commission this work. Every item below is a paraphrase of public Rave-owned material; URLs remain the source of record.

## Identity, proposition and pricing

- `rave-about` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/about — Rave describes itself as a coffee roaster seeking raw coffee of at least 82 SCA points for blends and 84+ for single origins. It explicitly positions its prices as unusually low for its quality, saying buyers should pay for coffee rather than expensive packaging. Its voice rejects corporate pedigree and coffee solemnity in favour of fun, personable service and a simple ambition to serve excellent coffee.
- `rave-home` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/ — The consumer storefront describes Rave as a UK speciality roaster, organised prominently around espresso-machine beans, filter beans and decaf. It offers blends, single origins, rare microlots, pods, organic coffee, equipment, syrup and gifts, and says orders are roasted fresh and dispatched the next working day.
- `rave-signature` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/products/signature-blend — Signature Blend No. 1 is called Rave's best seller, with caramel, almond and chocolate notes. On capture, 250g was £7.95 and 1kg £27.03; the product could be supplied as whole bean or ground for four named brewing methods. Free UK shipping began at £25.
- `rave-range` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/collections/all-roasted — The catalogue exposed 57 roast-filter results across blends, single origins, pods/bags and other formats. It spanned dark through light roast and familiar chocolate/caramel flavours through unusual fruit and floral profiles. This is a broad assortment, not evidence of the sales mix.
- `rave-rare` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/collections/rare-coffees-projects — The Rare range is positioned for black, slow-filter drinking and unusual processes, varietals and flavour. Captured prices for 250g-class products were roughly £12–£16, with one limited 150g co-ferment at £19.80. Several limited products were sold out; that indicates availability, not necessarily demand.

## Repeat, learning and customer progression

- `rave-coffee-subscription` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/coffee-subscription — Coffee Club starts at £9.95 with free tracked delivery. It promises an exclusive coffee each month plus education covering growing, roasting, brewing and tasting. Buyers choose Traditional, Discovery or mixed, grind and quantity; they may pause, skip or cancel. Gift terms run from three to twelve months.
- `rave-subscribe-save` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/collections/subscribe-save-10 — A distinct replenishment proposition offers 10% off chosen favourites at a selected frequency, with swapping, pausing, skipping and bringing delivery forward. It focuses on never running out, not discovery. Thus Rave operates at least two repeat jobs: dependable replenishment and guided exploration.
- `rave-rewards` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/rewards — The rewards scheme grants 3–6 points per pound, annual spend tiers at £75, £200 and £1,000, birthday rewards, vouchers and referral rewards. Points cannot be combined with other discounts, and applying rewards to a subscription currently requires customer-service intervention.
- `rave-quiz` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/coffee-quiz — Rave links prominently to a coffee quiz, but its dynamic question and recommendation logic was not visible in the retrieved public page. Its effectiveness and conversion role are unknown.

## Format and channel extensions

- `rave-pods` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/collections/compostable-nespresso-coffee-pods — Rave sells original-line Nespresso-compatible pods across blends, single origin and decaf. Captured ten-pod prices generally began at £4.20 before the stated 10% repeat discount. The collection calls the pods home-compostable.
- `rave-iced` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/products/iced-coffee-cans-ready-to-drink — Rave offers 250ml milk-based iced latte and caramel latte cans using its Signature blend and cold-brew coffee; a four-pack was £8.95 when captured. The product page showed the item as sold out, which is only a point-in-time availability signal.
- `rave-wholesale` — https://wholesale.ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/contact — Rave says it supplies cafes, restaurants, hotels, offices, co-working spaces and kiosks across the UK. The minimum is a box set at £86, described as equivalent to five 1kg bags of best sellers; wholesale partners receive free next-working-day dispatch, and orders before midday are normally roasted and dispatched the same day. Rave offers sampling at its Cirencester HQ.
- `rave-hq` — https://wholesale.ravecoffee.co.uk/ — The wholesale proposition includes coffee, equipment, installation, training and servicing, suggesting a service system as well as bean supply. The site says hundreds of UK businesses use Rave; this is a company claim and no customer count was independently verified.

## Environmental promise

- `rave-impact` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/1-for-the-planet — Rave says it donates 1% of sales, whether profitable or not, to environmental causes. Its public page displays separate cumulative trees/donation figures without dates or a clear total methodology, so the commitment is clearer than the impact accounting.

## Evidence limits from this extract

No source provides revenue by product/channel, contribution margin, CAC, retention, churn, repeat rate, cohort behaviour, wholesale concentration, unaided awareness, conversion, capacity utilisation or customer segmentation. Product prominence is not sales evidence. All Rave claims require management or third-party verification before being treated as operational truth.

# SAFE Rave Coffee public-evidence extract — market and competitors

Captured 2026-09-06 for internal strategic research only. Market sources are identified; competitor claims are their own and should not be treated as audited performance.

## UK market structure and pressure

- `cbi-uk-market-2026` — https://www.cbi.eu/market-information/coffee/united-kingdom/market-potential — CBI's 26 August 2026 update characterises the UK as a large, still-growing coffee consumption market where most growth is value-led premiumisation rather than volume. It calls the UK one of Europe's largest specialty markets and says ground coffee and single serve continue to gain popularity. It also records rapid RTD growth, while warning that the commercial role of coffee quality in RTD is uncertain.
- The same CBI source describes a polarisation: demand at the very top for scarce, experimental coffees, while cost-pressured buyers and operators shift towards lower-priced specialty blends. It calls out an eroding 84–86-point middle. This is directly relevant to Rave's accessible blends plus Rare range, but it does not prove Rave benefits from the pattern.
- The same source says UK green-coffee imports rose from 154,000 tonnes in 2024 to 165,000 in 2025, and cites almost 2,000 registered UK roasters. Those figures indicate supply and competitive density, not addressable demand for Rave.
- `world-coffee-portal-2025` — https://www.worldcoffeeportal.com/content/files/2025/06/The-Future-of-Coffee-UK-2025-infographic-2.pdf — A public one-page infographic reports only 8% of surveyed consumers willing to pay more than £5 for a premium beverage, rising to 12% under age 35. Half of surveyed industry respondents agreed it was a good time to sell specialty coffee in the UK. The underlying paid study, sample and methodology were not available, so this is directional only.
- `ico-public-market` — https://ico.org/resources/public-market-information/ — The International Coffee Organization reported a July 2026 composite price of 287.26 US cents/lb, up 15.4% from June. This is a current global raw-coffee price indicator, not Rave's input cost or hedging position.

## Competitive proposition and price comparison

- `pact-subscription` — https://www.pactcoffee.com/subscribe-and-save/select-plan — Pact's Select plan was £8.95 per 250g, rotates coffees across ten countries, invites preference ratings, and foregrounds payments above Fairtrade base price. Flexibility and free next-day delivery are prominent. Pact therefore competes on guided variety, farmer economics and convenience.
- `grind-subscription` — https://grind.co.uk/pages/coffee-subscription — Grind spans pods, bean, ground and cans; it foregrounds a 25% first-order reduction, a free branded tin, free shipping and “barista-quality” convenience. Captured starting monthly prices were £13.95 one-time / £10.46 promotional for pods and £14.95 / £11.21 for bean or ground. Its London café identity and distinctive reusable tin turn subscription into a visible lifestyle object.
- `origin-subscription` — https://www.origincoffee.co.uk/pages/coffee-subscriptions — Origin's Feature subscription was £12.95 and presents seasonality, provenance unavailable in supermarkets, B Corp credentials, sustainability awards and a new coffee each week. Its proof system is more overtly premium and specialist than Rave's accessible voice.
- `union-subscription` — https://unionroasted.com/products/discovery-coffee-subscription — Union's Discovery offer was £18.95 for two 200g bags, rotating monthly. It foregrounds Union Direct Trade, explicit quality scores and freshly roasted ethical sourcing. Union therefore makes sourcing methodology and coffee grading central choice cues.
- Rave's Coffee Club starting price of £9.95 sits near Pact and below the captured Origin/Union discovery offers, but weights and delivery cadence differ. This is not a like-for-like price index. Across all five brands, flexibility, fresh roasting, ethical sourcing and exploration recur, making them weak standalone differentiators.

## Behaviour and choice implications

- `british-coffee-association-consumption` — https://britishcoffeeassociation.org/coffee-consumption/ — The BCA states that 80% of UK households buy instant coffee and that ground coffee and single-serve formats are increasingly popular, especially among younger adults. The page's underlying dates are not transparent enough for precise market sizing; it supports only the broad observation that the conversion pool is larger than existing specialty buyers.
- Competitor navigation and offer architecture consistently start with consumption format, grind or plan selection. That is evidence of category practice, not evidence that it is the optimum architecture.

## Evidence limits from this extract

No source supplies comparable UK DTC market shares, subscription retention, CAC, branded search, price elasticity or channel profitability. Competitor prices are snapshots and package sizes differ. Search-volume evidence was not available from a reliable primary source. Strategic claims about switching or segment size must remain hypotheses.

# SAFE Rave Coffee public-evidence extract — directional customer signals

Captured 2026-09-06 for internal strategic research only. These are public, self-selected, unverified reviews. They are not a representative customer study and must never be attributed to Rave management.

- `rave-trustpilot-2026` — https://www.trustpilot.com/review/ravecoffee.co.uk — On capture, Rave's claimed Trustpilot profile showed 356 reviews and a 4.0/5 score; 75% were five-star and 13% one-star. Trustpilot notes that anyone may write and later edit a review, so these proportions are directional rather than population estimates.
- Positive 2026 reviews repeatedly described Rave as a step up from supermarket coffee, good value for fresh beans, easy to subscribe/pause, and supported by approachable human advice. One reviewer explicitly framed Signature Blend as only slightly dearer than Tesco Finest; another described using Rave after buying a premium espresso machine. These are individual accounts, not verified cohorts.
- Several July–August 2026 negative reviews alleged dispatch delays, status messages preceding actual roasting or Royal Mail handoff, and declining reliability. Other recent reviews reported fast delivery. This is conflicting evidence: there may be a reliability issue during growth, but review selection, fulfilment responsibility and prevalence are unknown.
- Some reviewers loved consistent familiar blends; others found a single origin flat or stale. This suggests the experience promise must cover both repeatable reassurance and adventurous quality, but sensory variance cannot be diagnosed from reviews alone.
- The public company replies visible on the page sometimes appeared mismatched to the complaint. It is unclear whether this reflects page extraction/order artefacts or actual response quality, so it should not support a strategic conclusion without direct verification.

## Evidence limits

No verified-purchase filter, raw review export or representative sampling was available. The useful signal is the language buyers volunteer—value, freshness, reliability, accessibility and easy repeat—not the incidence of each issue.

# SAFE Rave Coffee additional evidence — filed scale and investment indicators

Captured 2026-09-06 from the official Companies House iXBRL filing. These accounts were prepared under the small-company regime, are audit-exempt, and omit the income statement; they cannot establish revenue, growth rate or profitability.

- `companies-house-overview` — https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07384599 — Rave Coffee Limited, company 07384599, is active, incorporated 22 September 2010, registered in Cirencester and classified under SIC 10832, production of coffee and coffee substitutes. Latest filed accounts cover 31 December 2024.
- `companies-house-accounts-2024` — https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07384599/filing-history/MzQ4MjM0MTAwOGFkaXF6a2N4/document?format=xhtml&download=1 — At 31 December 2024, filed net assets were £2.272m versus £1.511m in 2023. Cash was £1.294m versus £0.698m; stocks £0.403m versus £0.393m; trade debtors £0.383m versus £0.110m; creditors due within one year £1.550m versus £0.942m.
- The same filing reports average employees increasing from 42 in 2023 to 61 in 2024. It records £646k of tangible fixed-asset additions in 2024, including £390k freehold property and £164k plant/equipment additions. These data support a fact of organisational and asset expansion, but not whether capacity is constrained, productive or profitable.
- The company did not deliver its statement of income and retained earnings. Any claim about sales, EBITDA, channel mix or unit economics remains unsupported.

## Consequential unknown

The combination of higher employee count, fixed-asset investment, receivables and short-term creditors could reflect growth and scaling, but only management accounts, capacity data and channel economics can show whether Rave should prioritise more demand, higher repeat, wholesale throughput, margin or operational reliability.

# SAFE Rave Coffee additional evidence — promise consistency and operations

Captured 2026-09-06. Public claims are compared rather than resolved.

- `rave-pods` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/collections/compostable-nespresso-coffee-pods — The current collection page repeatedly describes Rave's pods as home-compostable and says they may break down in a well-managed home compost bin in about 90 days.
- `rave-knowledge-base` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/knowledge-base — The current knowledge-base page instead repeatedly describes the pods as industrially compostable and directs users to food-waste collection, noting home compost may take longer. These statements are materially inconsistent for a buyer deciding disposal behaviour. The underlying certification was not located.
- `rave-impact` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/1-for-the-planet — The 1%-of-sales commitment is clear, but multiple displayed impact numbers lack dates, beneficiaries and a reconciled cumulative total. Competitors prominently use B Corp, direct-trade or named-foundation proof systems; Rave's environmental action may be real but its public proof is harder to audit from the surface reviewed.
- `rave-wholesale` — https://wholesale.ravecoffee.co.uk/pages/contact — Rave promises same-day roasting/dispatch before midday and free next-day wholesale dispatch. `rave-home` promises next-working-day consumer dispatch. Directional July–August 2026 Trustpilot reviews conflict on whether the promise was consistently met. This cannot establish an operational failure rate, but makes reliability a discovery question before scaling a promise built around freshness and convenience.

## Strategic significance to test

Rave's accessible voice depends on making specialty coffee easier, not introducing uncertainty about freshness, delivery or disposal. If these inconsistencies are isolated editorial issues, fix the proof layer. If they reflect operating strain, acquisition-led growth could amplify churn and service cost. Internal data is required to distinguish the two.

# SAFE Rave Coffee additional evidence — channel and proposition options

Captured 2026-09-06. These are observed public moves and comparative signals, not recommendations.

- `sparklayer-rave-case` — https://www.sparklayer.io/blog/2025/02/26/shopify-b2b-rave-coffee/ — Rave's B2B commerce supplier says Rave was primarily B2C but had a wholesale channel growing in importance, and implemented customer groups, B2B price lists, payment methods and order rules. This is a vendor case study and does not disclose audited sales, but supports the existence of deliberate wholesale infrastructure.
- `rave-wholesale` — https://wholesale.ravecoffee.co.uk/ — Rave combines coffee supply with equipment, installation, training and service across offices and hospitality. That creates recurring embedded relationships unlike anonymous DTC acquisition, but economics, retention and geographic service capacity are unknown.
- `rave-iced` — https://ravecoffee.co.uk/products/iced-coffee-cans-ready-to-drink — Rave has entered milk-based RTD using Signature Blend. `cbi-uk-market-2026` identifies RTD as fast-growing but cautions that coffee quality may play a small role in multi-ingredient products. Rave therefore has evidence of format expansion, not yet evidence that its speciality difference travels into RTD.
- `rave-owned-surface` — Rave's accessible core blends, pods, Coffee Club, Subscribe & Save, rare microlots, equipment, gifts, wholesale service and RTD collectively cover many jobs. The range can serve progression from supermarket upgrader to enthusiast, but the public site does not express that progression as one ownable system.
- Competitor comparison: Pact owns farmer fairness and personalisation; Origin owns expert provenance and premium credentials; Grind owns visible urban lifestyle, pods and format; Union owns direct trade and quality proof. Rave's most distinctive stated combination is accessible price, irreverent non-judgement, breadth across how people brew, and personable help. Whether customers recognise and value that combination is unproven.

## Decision tests enabled by this evidence

1. Does Rave win disproportionately when a buyer has just upgraded equipment or wants to leave supermarket coffee, rather than when an enthusiast seeks maximum novelty?
2. Can Rave organise its range as a confidence-building progression—dependable everyday anchor, guided exploration, rare frontier—without discounting or flattening its specialist credibility?
3. Is wholesale the faster route to repeated trial and local salience, or does its service burden constrain profitable scale?
4. Does RTD recruit people into Rave's coffee system, or dilute the brand into a generic growing format?

Only customer cohorts, channel economics and conversion paths can resolve these questions.
